title: Probably Approximately Correct Constrained Learning
authors: Luiz F. O. Chamon and Alejandro Ribeiro
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 33
conclusions: Extends the PAC learning framework to constrained learning (PACC), formalizing constrained ERM (P-ECRM) and proving that any PAC-learnable hypothesis class is also PAC-constrained learnable (Thm 1), i.e. constraints don't make learning statistically harder.

Shows the empirical dual problem of a parametrized constrained ERM is a near-PACC learner (Thm 2), with an approximation error tied to the richness of the parametrization and the strictness of the constraints.

Derives a practical primal-dual (sub)gradient algorithm (Algorithm 1: train primal via an oracle, then do dual-ascent multiplier updates each 'epoch') with a convergence-to-neighborhood guarantee (Thm 3).

Demonstrates the framework on two illustrations: fair classification on the Adult dataset (average + pointwise KL-invariance constraints) and adversarially robust classification on FashionMNIST via a constrained (not fixed-penalty) robustness formulation.

Positions constrained learning as generically preferable to fixed-weight regularization because constraint levels are directly interpretable and dual variables carry a sensitivity/fairness diagnostic (Fig 1b).

Is a theory paper: no notion of transductive/test-set count constraints, no rare-class caps, no bounded/saturating penalty, no multiplier-freeze-at-satisfaction or optimizer-reset mechanisms -- it uses a plain dual-ascent multiplier that can grow, contributed instead as prior statistical/practical grounding for the classical Lagrangian recipe.
our_use: main.tex:92 cites it (with fioretto2020lagrangian, hounie2023resilient) for 'solve the Lagrangian with dual ascent' as the constrained-training baseline family whose multiplier climbs unboundedly under a hard cap -- matches Algorithm 1's plain projected dual-ascent update with no freeze/reset mechanism. main.tex:155 cites it (with chamon2023constrained) for giving 'statistical footing by PAC constrained-learning theory' to Lagrangian-duality training -- matches the paper's core PACC/near-PACC generalization results (Thm 1-3).
